title: CTS Unit 11 — The Prosperity Gospel and Other Excesses / El evangelio de la prosperidad y otros excesos

blocks.en: Pentecostalism & the Charismatic Movement · Unit 11
blocks.es_reference: El pentecostalismo y el movimiento carismático · Unidad 11

blocks.en: The Prosperity Gospel and Other Excesses
blocks.es_reference: El evangelio de la prosperidad y otros excesos

blocks.en: A Biblical Study · New King James Version
blocks.es_reference: Un estudio bíblico · Reina-Valera Gómez

blocks.en: "Now godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out."1 Timothy 6:6–7 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Pero gran ganancia es la piedad con contentamiento. Porque nada hemos traído a este mundo, y sin duda nada podremos sacar."1 Timoteo 6:6–7 (RVG)

blocks.en: Learning Objectives
blocks.es_reference: Objetivos de aprendizaje

blocks.en: Identify the grain of truth the prosperity gospel seizes upon and the specific points at which it distorts that truth.
blocks.es_reference: Identificar el grano de verdad del que se apodera el evangelio de la prosperidad y los puntos específicos en que distorsiona esa verdad.

blocks.en: Weigh the prosperity teaching by Scripture on wealth, faith, and suffering.
blocks.es_reference: Sopesar la enseñanza de la prosperidad por la Escritura en cuanto a la riqueza, la fe y el sufrimiento.

blocks.en: Recognize the pastoral harm the teaching does and respond with biblical comfort.
blocks.es_reference: Reconocer el daño pastoral que hace la enseñanza y responder con consuelo bíblico.

blocks.en: Name other common excesses and the New Testament remedies that correct them.
blocks.es_reference: Nombrar otros excesos comunes y los remedios del Nuevo Testamento que los corrigen.

blocks.en: Distinguish the distortion from the wider movement, judging a teaching by the Word and a movement by its Scriptures and its faithful.
blocks.es_reference: Distinguir la distorsión del movimiento más amplio, juzgando una enseñanza por la Palabra y un movimiento por sus Escrituras y sus fieles.

blocks.en: What This Unit Faces
blocks.es_reference: Lo que esta unidad enfrenta

blocks.en: To study a movement honestly is to face its distortions as well as its fruit. The most widespread distortion that has grown up around the Pentecostal and charismatic world is the teaching often called the "prosperity gospel," or the "health-and-wealth" message: the promise that God wills every believer to be rich and well, and that faith, rightly exercised, secures it.
blocks.es_reference: Estudiar un movimiento con honestidad es enfrentar sus distorsiones tanto como su fruto. La distorsión más extendida que ha crecido en torno al mundo pentecostal y carismático es la enseñanza a menudo llamada el "evangelio de la prosperidad," o el mensaje de "salud y riqueza": la promesa de que Dios quiere que todo creyente sea rico y sano, y que la fe, bien ejercida, lo asegura.

blocks.en: We will do two things in this unit, and we must do both at once. We will name the error plainly, testing it by Scripture. And we will refuse to lay that error at the door of the whole movement, the great majority of whom neither preach it nor believe it. The course's habit of keeping two questions apart serves us again here. One question is whether the teaching is biblical — and that we can answer. Another is whether an entire movement should be condemned for it — and to that the answer is no. Judge the teaching by the Word; judge the movement by its Scriptures and its faithful.
blocks.es_reference: Haremos dos cosas en esta unidad, y debemos hacer ambas a la vez. Nombraremos el error con claridad, probándolo por la Escritura. Y rehusaremos poner ese error a la puerta de todo el movimiento, cuya gran mayoría ni lo predica ni lo cree. El hábito del curso de mantener dos preguntas separadas nos sirve otra vez aquí. Una pregunta es si la enseñanza es bíblica — y eso podemos responderlo. Otra es si un movimiento entero debe ser condenado por ella — y a eso la respuesta es no. Juzgue la enseñanza por la Palabra; juzgue el movimiento por sus Escrituras y sus fieles.

blocks.en: The Grain of Truth
blocks.es_reference: El grano de verdad

blocks.en: A false teaching rarely spreads on lies alone; it spreads because it seizes on something true and stretches it out of shape. Honesty compels us to grant the grain of truth before we expose the distortion. God is a generous Father who delights to give good gifts to His children (Matt 7:11). He teaches us to pray for daily bread (Matt 6:11), which means our ordinary needs are His concern and not beneath His notice. He does heal, and He does provide; sickness and poverty are not His original design but intruders that came with the Fall, and they will have no place in the world to come.
blocks.es_reference: Una enseñanza falsa rara vez se difunde solo con mentiras; se difunde porque se apodera de algo verdadero y lo estira hasta deformarlo. La honestidad nos obliga a conceder el grano de verdad antes de exponer la distorsión. Dios es un Padre generoso que se deleita en dar buenas dádivas a sus hijos (Mt 7:11). Nos enseña a pedir el pan de cada día (Mt 6:11), lo cual significa que nuestras necesidades ordinarias son de su interés y no están por debajo de su atención. Él sí sana, y sí provee; la enfermedad y la pobreza no son su diseño original, sino intrusas que entraron con la Caída, y no tendrán lugar en el mundo venidero.

blocks.en: Scripture even joins generosity to blessing: "God is able to make all grace abound toward you" (2 Cor 9:8), and the one who gives is promised that it will be given back to him (Luke 6:38). None of this is in dispute. The prosperity teacher begins, as many errors do, with a truth in his hand. The trouble lies in what he adds to it.
blocks.es_reference: La Escritura aun une la generosidad a la bendición: "Dios es poderoso para hacer que abunde en vosotros toda gracia" (2 Cor 9:8), y al que da se le promete que le será devuelto (Lc 6:38). Nada de esto está en disputa. El maestro de la prosperidad comienza, como muchos errores, con una verdad en la mano. El problema está en lo que le añade.

blocks.en: Where the Distortion Begins
blocks.es_reference: Donde comienza la distorsión

blocks.en: The distortion is not in believing that God provides, but in the terms the teaching attaches to His provision. It says, first, that health and wealth are guaranteed to every believer as a covenant right, so that continued sickness or poverty is abnormal and ought never to be accepted. It says, second, that faith is a kind of force or formula — that if a person believes hard enough, or speaks the right words, God is obliged to deliver. This is the root of "positive confession," the notion that our words carry creative power to call things into being.
blocks.es_reference: La distorsión no está en creer que Dios provee, sino en los términos que la enseñanza adjunta a su provisión. Dice, primero, que la salud y la riqueza están garantizadas a todo creyente como un derecho del pacto, de modo que la enfermedad o la pobreza que continúan son anormales y jamás deberían aceptarse. Dice, segundo, que la fe es una especie de fuerza o fórmula — que si una persona cree con suficiente firmeza, o pronuncia las palabras correctas, Dios queda obligado a cumplir. Esta es la raíz de la "confesión positiva," la noción de que nuestras palabras llevan poder creador para llamar las cosas a la existencia.

blocks.en: It says, third, that giving money is a technique for securing return: sow a financial "seed," especially into the teacher's ministry, and reap a multiplied harvest. And it says, fourth and most cruelly, that when the health or wealth does not come, the fault lies in the believer's weak faith or hidden sin. Each of these turns a Father into a vending machine and faith into a lever for moving His hand. It is precisely here that Scripture parts company with the teaching.
blocks.es_reference: Dice, tercero, que dar dinero es una técnica para asegurar retorno: siembre una "semilla" financiera, sobre todo en el ministerio del maestro, y coseche una cosecha multiplicada. Y dice, cuarto y más cruelmente, que cuando la salud o la riqueza no llegan, la culpa está en la fe débil o el pecado oculto del creyente. Cada uno de estos convierte al Padre en una máquina expendedora y a la fe en una palanca para mover su mano. Es precisamente aquí donde la Escritura se aparta de la enseñanza.

blocks.en: Weighed in the Scriptures
blocks.es_reference: Sopesado en las Escrituras

blocks.en: Set beside the Word, the prosperity gospel is found wanting at every one of these points. Scripture does not present riches as the goal of the godly life but warns of their danger:
blocks.es_reference: Puesto junto a la Palabra, el evangelio de la prosperidad resulta falto en cada uno de estos puntos. La Escritura no presenta las riquezas como la meta de la vida piadosa, sino que advierte de su peligro:

blocks.en: "But those who desire to be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and harmful lusts which drown men in destruction and perdition. For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil."1 Timothy 6:9–10 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Porque los que quieren enriquecerse caen en tentación y lazo, y en muchas codicias necias y dañosas, que hunden a los hombres en destrucción y perdición. Porque raíz de todos los males es el amor al dinero."1 Timoteo 6:9–10 (RVG)

blocks.en: The Lord Himself set the tone this teaching reverses. He told His disciples not to lay up treasures on earth but treasures in heaven, “for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also” (Matt 6:19–21), and warned plainly, “You cannot serve God and mammon” (Matt 6:24). He told a parable of a rich man who filled his barns and lost his soul that very night (Luke 12:16–21), and He let a wealthy young ruler walk away sorrowful rather than soften the cost of following Him. None of this makes money evil or poverty holy; but it does mean that abundance is nowhere treated as the badge of God's favor, and that a heart set on gain stands in spiritual danger, not spiritual health.
blocks.es_reference: El Señor mismo marcó el tono que esta enseñanza invierte. Dijo a sus discípulos que no acumularan tesoros en la tierra sino tesoros en el cielo, “porque donde esté vuestro tesoro, allí estará también vuestro corazón” (Mt 6:19–21), y advirtió con claridad: “No podéis servir a Dios y a las riquezas” (Mt 6:24). Contó la parábola de un rico que llenó sus graneros y perdió su alma esa misma noche (Lc 12:16–21), y dejó marchar entristecido a un joven rico antes que suavizar el costo de seguirle. Nada de esto hace malo el dinero ni santa la pobreza; pero sí significa que la abundancia en ninguna parte se trata como la insignia del favor de Dios, y que un corazón puesto en la ganancia está en peligro espiritual, no en salud espiritual.

blocks.en: The Lord Jesus and His apostles were not men of wealth. The Son of Man had "nowhere to lay His head" (Matt 8:20); Paul knew hunger and need and learned to be content whether he had plenty or little (Phil 4:11–12). Nor does the New Testament exclude suffering from the believer's path; it promises it:
blocks.es_reference: El Señor Jesús y sus apóstoles no fueron hombres de riqueza. El Hijo del Hombre no tenía "dónde recostar su cabeza" (Mt 8:20); Pablo conoció el hambre y la necesidad y aprendió a contentarse ya tuviera mucho o poco (Flp 4:11–12). Tampoco el Nuevo Testamento excluye el sufrimiento del camino del creyente; lo promete:

blocks.en: "Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution."2 Timothy 3:12 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Y también todos los que quieren vivir piadosamente en Cristo Jesús, padecerán persecución."2 Timoteo 3:12 (RVG)

blocks.en: We are heirs of God, Paul writes, "if indeed we suffer with Him, that we may also be glorified together" (Rom 8:17); the road to glory runs through the cross, not around it. And faith itself is not a technique for bending God to our wishes but trust in His good will. Christ in Gethsemane prayed, "not My will, but Yours, be done" (Luke 22:42). When Paul pleaded three times for his thorn to be taken away, it was not removed; the answer he received was better than removal:
blocks.es_reference: Somos herederos de Dios, escribe Pablo, "si es que padecemos juntamente con él, para que juntamente con él seamos glorificados" (Ro 8:17); el camino a la gloria pasa por la cruz, no la rodea. Y la fe misma no es una técnica para doblegar a Dios a nuestros deseos, sino confianza en su buena voluntad. Cristo en Getsemaní oró: "no se haga mi voluntad, sino la tuya" (Lc 22:42). Cuando Pablo suplicó tres veces que le fuese quitado su aguijón, no fue quitado; la respuesta que recibió fue mejor que la remoción:

blocks.en: "My grace is sufficient for you, for My strength is made perfect in weakness."2 Corinthians 12:9 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Bástate mi gracia; porque mi poder se perfecciona en la debilidad."2 Corintios 12:9 (RVG)

blocks.en: Paul even warns Timothy against those "who suppose that godliness is a means of gain" (1 Tim 6:5). The prosperity gospel, then, misreads the very shape of the Christian life.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo aun advierte a Timoteo contra los que "toman la piedad por fuente de ganancia" (1 Tim 6:5). El evangelio de la prosperidad, entonces, lee mal la forma misma de la vida cristiana.

blocks.en: It is worth seeing how the teaching handles the very verses it leans on, for it reads each against its plain sense. It takes the apostle John's warm greeting, a wish that his friend may “prosper and be in health” (3 John 2), and turns a first-century letter's courtesy into a universal financial promise. It takes “by His stripes we are healed” (Isa 53:5; 1 Pet 2:24), which the context ties to the healing of our souls from sin, and presses it into a guarantee of bodily cure on demand. It lifts the covenant blessings promised to Israel under the Law (Deut 28) out of their setting and reassigns them wholesale to the believer's bank account. It even presses Malachi's promise that God will “open the windows of heaven” for the tithe (Mal 3:10) into a money-back guarantee, as though giving were an investment with a contractual return rather than an act of worship and trust. In each case a text is bent to serve a system it was never given to support.
blocks.es_reference: Vale la pena ver cómo la enseñanza maneja los mismos versículos en que se apoya, pues lee cada uno en contra de su sentido llano. Toma el cálido saludo del apóstol Juan, un deseo de que su amigo sea “prosperado en todas las cosas, y que tenga salud” (3 Jn 2), y convierte la cortesía de una carta del primer siglo en una promesa financiera universal. Toma “por su llaga fuimos nosotros curados” (Is 53:5; 1 P 2:24), que el contexto liga a la sanidad de nuestras almas del pecado, y la fuerza hasta hacerla una garantía de cura corporal a demanda. Levanta las bendiciones del pacto prometidas a Israel bajo la Ley (Dt 28) fuera de su marco y las reasigna por entero a la cuenta bancaria del creyente. Aun fuerza la promesa de Malaquías de que Dios abrirá “las ventanas de los cielos” por el diezmo (Mal 3:10) hasta hacerla una garantía de devolución, como si dar fuera una inversión con retorno contractual y no un acto de adoración y confianza. En cada caso un texto es torcido para servir a un sistema que nunca le fue dado para sostener.

blocks.en: The Pastoral Wound
blocks.es_reference: La herida pastoral

blocks.en: This is no mere debate over doctrine; it wounds real people, and a pastor must feel the wound before he answers it. Consider the believer told that his cancer persists because his faith is too weak. Consider the widow who gave her last coins expecting a hundredfold return and received nothing but deeper poverty. Consider the parents taught that a stillborn child, or an empty cupboard, is a verdict on their walk with God. To grief and sickness such teaching adds a second cruelty: it blames the afflicted for their affliction.
blocks.es_reference: Esto no es un mero debate sobre doctrina; hiere a personas reales, y un pastor debe sentir la herida antes de responderla. Considere al creyente a quien se le dice que su cáncer persiste porque su fe es demasiado débil. Considere a la viuda que dio sus últimas monedas esperando un retorno del ciento por uno y no recibió sino una pobreza más honda. Considere a los padres a quienes se enseña que un niño que nace muerto, o una alacena vacía, es un veredicto sobre su andar con Dios. Al dolor y a la enfermedad tal enseñanza añade una segunda crueldad: culpa al afligido por su aflicción.

blocks.en: The Scriptures speak the opposite word. "The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart" (Ps 34:18). Job's long agony was not the punishment of a secret sin, as his friends wrongly insisted. And when the disciples asked whose sin had caused a man's blindness, the Lord refused the whole premise:
blocks.es_reference: Las Escrituras hablan la palabra contraria. "Cercano está Jehová a los quebrantados de corazón" (Sal 34:18). La larga agonía de Job no fue el castigo de un pecado secreto, como sus amigos insistían erróneamente. Y cuando los discípulos preguntaron de quién era el pecado que había causado la ceguera de un hombre, el Señor rechazó toda la premisa:

blocks.en: "Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but that the works of God should be revealed in him."John 9:3 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "No es que pecó éste, ni sus padres, sino para que las obras de Dios se manifiesten en él."Juan 9:3 (RVG)

blocks.en: A shepherd of Christ's flock guards his people from any message that reads their suffering as a sentence, and points them instead to the God who is nearest when the heart is most broken.
blocks.es_reference: Un pastor del rebaño de Cristo guarda a su gente de todo mensaje que lea su sufrimiento como una sentencia, y en cambio los señala al Dios que está más cerca cuando el corazón está más quebrantado.

blocks.en: Other Excesses
blocks.es_reference: Otros excesos

blocks.en: The prosperity teaching is the most far-reaching distortion, but it is not the only one, and the same discipline meets them all. There is the manipulation of emotion and of the offering, where feeling is worked up and pressure applied until people give what they cannot afford. There is the elevation of celebrity leaders above correction, gathering to themselves an authority no man should hold alone. There are claimed prophecies that fail and are quietly forgotten rather than honestly owned. There is the manufacturing of experiences, and the confusion of noise and excitement with the moving of the Spirit.
blocks.es_reference: La enseñanza de la prosperidad es la distorsión de mayor alcance, pero no es la única, y la misma disciplina las enfrenta a todas. Está la manipulación de la emoción y de la ofrenda, donde se aviva el sentimiento y se aplica presión hasta que la gente da lo que no puede permitirse. Está la elevación de líderes célebres por encima de la corrección, atrayendo hacia sí una autoridad que ningún hombre debería tener solo. Están las profecías reclamadas que fallan y se olvidan calladamente en vez de reconocerse con honestidad. Está la fabricación de experiencias, y la confusión del ruido y la excitación con el mover del Espíritu.

blocks.en: The New Testament's remedies do not change from case to case. Test all things and hold fast what is good, as the previous unit urged (1 Thess 5:21). Keep a plurality of elders and mutual accountability, so that no leader stands beyond reach. Handle money with transparent integrity, "providing honorable things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men" (2 Cor 8:21). Excess is not cured by quenching the Spirit but by submitting every practice to the Word.
blocks.es_reference: Los remedios del Nuevo Testamento no cambian de un caso a otro. Examinar todas las cosas y retener lo bueno, como urgió la unidad anterior (1 Ts 5:21). Mantener una pluralidad de ancianos y rendición mutua de cuentas, para que ningún líder quede fuera de alcance. Manejar el dinero con integridad transparente, "procurando hacer las cosas honradamente, no solo delante del Señor, sino también delante de los hombres" (2 Cor 8:21). El exceso no se cura apagando al Espíritu, sino sometiendo cada práctica a la Palabra.

blocks.en: Against the manipulated offering, Scripture sets a picture of giving that is glad and free: “So let each one give as he purposes in his heart, not grudgingly or of necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver” (2 Cor 9:7). The Spirit does not need the pressure of the fund-raiser or the theatrics of the stage; true worship and true generosity flow from a willing heart, not from fear or the hope of a payout. When a ministry must manufacture excitement or lean hard on people's pockets to sustain itself, that is itself a warning sign. The remedy for hollow excess is never less of the Spirit but more of the Word, and more of the quiet fruit the Spirit actually produces — love, joy, peace, patience, and self-control.
blocks.es_reference: Contra la ofrenda manipulada, la Escritura pone un cuadro del dar que es alegre y libre: “Cada uno dé como propuso en su corazón, no con tristeza, ni por necesidad, porque Dios ama al dador alegre” (2 Cor 9:7). El Espíritu no necesita la presión del recaudador ni la teatralidad del escenario; la verdadera adoración y la verdadera generosidad brotan de un corazón dispuesto, no del miedo ni de la esperanza de un pago. Cuando un ministerio debe fabricar excitación o apretar con fuerza los bolsillos de la gente para sostenerse, eso mismo es una señal de alarma. El remedio para el exceso hueco nunca es menos del Espíritu sino más de la Palabra, y más del fruto callado que el Espíritu de veras produce — amor, gozo, paz, paciencia y templanza.

blocks.en: Not the Whole Movement
blocks.es_reference: No todo el movimiento

blocks.en: Having named these things plainly, we must now say, with equal firmness, what would be unjust to leave unsaid: these distortions are not the faith of the whole Pentecostal and charismatic movement, and it is neither fair nor true to charge them to it. The great majority of the movement's hundreds of millions are ordinary believers in modest churches and poor villages, who have never preached health-and-wealth and would not recognize it as the gospel they trust.
blocks.es_reference: Habiendo nombrado estas cosas con claridad, ahora debemos decir, con igual firmeza, lo que sería injusto callar: estas distorsiones no son la fe de todo el movimiento pentecostal y carismático, y no es ni justo ni verdadero cargárselas. La gran mayoría de los cientos de millones del movimiento son creyentes ordinarios en iglesias modestas y aldeas pobres, que nunca han predicado salud y riqueza y no lo reconocerían como el evangelio en que confían.

blocks.en: The same movement has sent out tireless evangelists to the hardest fields, faithful missionaries who embraced poverty for the sake of the call, and martyrs who suffered and died for Christ — men and women whose lives are the very opposite of a gospel of ease and gain. A teaching is to be judged on its own terms, by Scripture; a movement is to be judged by its Scriptures and by its faithful, not by its worst and most visible preachers. Indeed, we reject the distortion for the same reason its own faithful people reject it: because it is not the gospel of the crucified and risen Lord. To condemn the many for the errors of a few would only add a second injustice to the first.
blocks.es_reference: El mismo movimiento ha enviado evangelistas incansables a los campos más duros, misioneros fieles que abrazaron la pobreza por causa del llamado, y mártires que sufrieron y murieron por Cristo — hombres y mujeres cuyas vidas son lo opuesto mismo de un evangelio de comodidad y ganancia. Una enseñanza ha de juzgarse por sí misma, por la Escritura; un movimiento ha de juzgarse por sus Escrituras y por sus fieles, no por sus peores y más visibles predicadores. En verdad, rechazamos la distorsión por la misma razón que su propia gente fiel la rechaza: porque no es el evangelio del Señor crucificado y resucitado. Condenar a los muchos por los errores de unos pocos solo añadiría una segunda injusticia a la primera.

blocks.en: It is worth adding that the movement has not been silent about its own distortions. Pentecostal and charismatic theologians, pastors, and even official denominational statements have publicly rejected the prosperity message and the excesses of positive confession as a corruption of the gospel of grace. The sharpest critics of health-and-wealth teaching are often found not outside the movement but within it, among believers who love the work of the Spirit and grieve to see His name attached to a message of mere gain. A body that names and disowns the error in its own midst is showing the marks of health, not sickness. This too is a reason to weigh the movement by its faithful and by its Scriptures, and to refuse the easy caricature that paints the whole with the colors of its worst.
blocks.es_reference: Vale la pena añadir que el movimiento no ha callado sobre sus propias distorsiones. Teólogos, pastores y aun declaraciones denominacionales oficiales del mundo pentecostal y carismático han rechazado públicamente el mensaje de la prosperidad y los excesos de la confesión positiva como una corrupción del evangelio de la gracia. Los críticos más agudos de la enseñanza de salud y riqueza a menudo se hallan no fuera del movimiento sino dentro de él, entre creyentes que aman la obra del Espíritu y se duelen de ver su nombre atado a un mensaje de mera ganancia. Un cuerpo que nombra y repudia el error en su propio seno muestra señales de salud, no de enfermedad. También esto es razón para sopesar el movimiento por sus fieles y sus Escrituras, y para rehusar la caricatura fácil que pinta al todo con los colores de sus peores.

blocks.en: Holding Truth and Charity Together
blocks.es_reference: Sosteniendo juntas la verdad y la caridad

blocks.en: So we hold two things together that are often torn apart. We name the error without contempt, and we warn the flock without slandering our brothers. We refuse the false riches that cannot satisfy and cannot last, and we hold out the true riches in their place: Christ Himself, and "godliness with contentment," which is gain no thief can reach and no illness can cancel. The Spirit of God was given to glorify Christ, not to enrich those who speak in His name; and the surest mark of the Spirit's true work is not a fuller wallet but a heart content in God and generous toward others.
blocks.es_reference: Así sostenemos juntas dos cosas que a menudo se separan. Nombramos el error sin desprecio, y advertimos al rebaño sin calumniar a nuestros hermanos. Rehusamos las riquezas falsas que no pueden satisfacer ni durar, y en su lugar ofrecemos las verdaderas riquezas: Cristo mismo, y "la piedad con contentamiento," que es una ganancia que ningún ladrón alcanza y ninguna enfermedad cancela. El Espíritu de Dios fue dado para glorificar a Cristo, no para enriquecer a los que hablan en su nombre; y la señal más segura de la verdadera obra del Espíritu no es una billetera más llena, sino un corazón contento en Dios y generoso con los demás.

blocks.en: Looking Ahead
blocks.es_reference: Mirando adelante

blocks.en: One unit remains. Having studied the movement's history, its gifts, and its distortions, we will draw the threads together into a biblical assessment of the whole: what the church may gladly affirm, what it must decline, and how to separate the genuine gift from the counterfeit that so often grows up beside it.
blocks.es_reference: Queda una unidad. Habiendo estudiado la historia del movimiento, sus dones y sus distorsiones, uniremos los hilos en una evaluación bíblica del conjunto: lo que la iglesia puede afirmar con gozo, lo que debe declinar, y cómo separar el don genuino de la falsificación que tan a menudo crece a su lado.

blocks.en: Discussion Questions
blocks.es_reference: Preguntas para discusión

blocks.en: Where is the "grain of truth" in the prosperity impulse, and where exactly does it become distortion?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Dónde está el "grano de verdad" en el impulso de la prosperidad, y dónde exactamente se vuelve distorsión?

mc.stem: Alongside naming the prosperity gospel's error, this unit is equally careful to —
options: condemn the entire Pentecostal and charismatic movement for it
avoid quoting Scripture at all
refuse to charge the distortion to the whole movement, most of whom reject it
declare all giving of money sinful
mc.why: A teaching is judged on its own by the Word; a movement by its Scriptures and its faithful — so the error is named without condemning the many who reject it.

mc.stem: The grain of truth the prosperity impulse seizes upon is that —
options: God guarantees every believer wealth
faith is a force that compels God
sickness always proves hidden sin
God is a generous Father who provides for His children and does heal
mc.why: The teaching gains a hearing by seizing on real truths — God's generosity and provision — before stretching them out of shape.

mc.stem: The distortion begins when the teaching adds that —
options: God cares about our daily needs
health and wealth are guaranteed rights, faith is a formula, and sickness or poverty proves too little faith
believers should be generous
God is good and kind
mc.why: The error lies not in trusting God's provision but in the terms added: guaranteed wealth, faith as a lever, and blame on the afflicted.

options: those who desire to be rich fall into a snare, and the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil
godliness is a means of financial gain
the rich are the most faithful believers
contentment is worthless
mc.why: 1 Timothy 6:9–10 makes riches a danger, not a goal, and lifts up godliness with contentment as the true gain.

mc.stem: On suffering, the New Testament teaches that —
options: true faith removes all hardship
sickness is always a verdict on sin
Christ promised His followers ease
all who desire to live godly will suffer persecution, and we are heirs if indeed we suffer with Him
mc.why: 2 Timothy 3:12 and Romans 8:17 place the believer's road through the cross, not around it.

mc.stem: When Paul asked three times for his thorn to be removed, God's answer was —
options: that Paul plainly lacked faith
to remove it at once as a reward
My grace is sufficient for you, for My strength is made perfect in weakness
complete silence
mc.why: 2 Corinthians 12:9 shows faith as trust in God's will, not a technique that guarantees relief.

mc.stem: A movement, this unit argues, must be judged —
options: by its Scriptures and its faithful, while a teaching is judged on its own terms by the Word
by its worst and most famous preachers
by its television programs
not at all
mc.why: To charge the distortion to the whole movement would be unjust; the many faithful reject it for the same reason we do.

sa.prompt: State the two things this unit is careful to do at once when it addresses the prosperity gospel, and why both matter.
sa.model: The unit is careful to do two things at once: to name the error of the prosperity gospel plainly by Scripture, and to refuse to charge that error to the whole Pentecostal and charismatic movement, most of whom reject it. Both matter because a teaching must be judged on its own terms by the Word, while a movement must be judged by its Scriptures and its faithful, not by its worst preachers; to condemn the many for the distortion of a few would be unjust and untrue.

sa.prompt: Give three ways Scripture corrects the prosperity gospel's view of faith, wealth, and suffering.
sa.model: First, Scripture treats the love of money as a snare, not a goal, and holds up godliness with contentment as the true gain. Second, it promises suffering rather than excluding it: all who live godly will face persecution, and Christ himself had nowhere to lay his head. Third, it shows faith as trust in God's will rather than a technique to bend it: Paul's thorn was left in place and the answer was grace, God's strength made perfect in weakness. So wealth is no proof of favor and hardship is no proof of unbelief.

sa.prompt: Explain how a pastor should warn against the prosperity gospel and other excesses without wounding faithful believers.
sa.model: A pastor should name the error clearly but without contempt, warning the flock while refusing to slander the many faithful believers who reject it. He must guard the afflicted from a message that blames them for their sickness or poverty, remembering that suffering is not a verdict on sin. Against other excesses he applies the same biblical remedies: test all things, keep a plurality of elders and mutual accountability, and handle money with integrity. Truth and charity are held together, so that error is opposed and brothers are honored.

sa.prompt: State the four terms the prosperity teaching attaches to God's provision, and what they turn the Father and faith into.
sa.model: First, that health and wealth are guaranteed to every believer as a covenant right, so continued sickness or poverty is abnormal. Second, that faith is a force or formula, so that believing hard enough or speaking the right words obliges God to deliver, the root of 'positive confession'. Third, that giving money is a technique for return, sowing a financial seed, especially into the teacher's ministry, to reap a multiplied harvest. Fourth and most cruelly, that when health or wealth does not come, the fault lies in the believer's weak faith or hidden sin. Each turns a Father into a vending machine and faith into a lever for moving His hand.

sa.prompt: How did the Lord Jesus set the tone that the prosperity teaching reverses, on treasure, mammon, and riches?
sa.model: He told His disciples not to lay up treasures on earth but in heaven, for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also, and warned that you cannot serve God and mammon (Matthew 6). He told the parable of the rich man who filled his barns and lost his soul that very night, and He let a wealthy young ruler walk away sorrowful rather than soften the cost of following Him. None of this makes money evil or poverty holy, but abundance is nowhere treated as the badge of God's favor, and a heart set on gain stands in spiritual danger, not spiritual health.

sa.prompt: What do the lives of Jesus and Paul, and 2 Timothy 3:12 and Romans 8:17, show about wealth and suffering in the Christian life?
sa.model: The Lord and His apostles were not men of wealth: the Son of Man had nowhere to lay His head, and Paul knew hunger and need and learned to be content with plenty or little. The New Testament does not exclude suffering from the believer's path but promises it, 'all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution', and we are heirs of God 'if indeed we suffer with Him', so the road to glory runs through the cross, not around it. Paul even warns Timothy against those who suppose that godliness is a means of gain; the prosperity gospel misreads the very shape of the Christian life.

sa.prompt: Show how the prosperity teaching bends the verses it leans on: 3 John 2, Isaiah 53:5, Deuteronomy 28, and Malachi 3:10.
sa.model: It takes John's warm greeting, a wish that his friend may prosper and be in health (3 John 2), and turns a first-century letter's courtesy into a universal financial promise. It takes 'by His stripes we are healed', which the context ties to the healing of our souls from sin, and presses it into a guarantee of bodily cure on demand. It lifts the covenant blessings promised to Israel under the Law (Deuteronomy 28) out of their setting and reassigns them to the believer's bank account. And it presses Malachi's promise to open the windows of heaven for the tithe into a money-back guarantee, as though giving were an investment with a contractual return rather than an act of worship and trust. In each case a text is bent to serve a system it was never given to support.

sa.prompt: Name the 'other excesses' the unit lists and the New Testament remedies it prescribes.
sa.model: The manipulation of emotion and of the offering, where feeling is worked up and pressure applied until people give what they cannot afford; the elevation of celebrity leaders above correction; claimed prophecies that fail and are quietly forgotten; and the manufacturing of experiences, confusing noise and excitement with the moving of the Spirit. The remedies do not change: test all things and hold fast what is good; keep a plurality of elders and mutual accountability so no leader stands beyond reach; handle money with transparent integrity, providing honorable things in the sight of the Lord and of men; and set against the manipulated offering the glad, free giving of the cheerful giver. Excess is cured not by quenching the Spirit but by submitting every practice to the Word.

sa.prompt: Why is it unjust to charge the prosperity gospel to the whole movement, and what evidence does the unit give?
sa.model: The great majority of the movement's hundreds of millions are ordinary believers in modest churches and poor villages who have never preached health-and-wealth and would not recognize it as the gospel they trust. The same movement has sent out tireless evangelists to the hardest fields, missionaries who embraced poverty for the sake of the call, and martyrs who suffered and died for Christ, lives that are the very opposite of a gospel of ease and gain. A teaching is judged by Scripture; a movement by its Scriptures and its faithful, not by its worst and most visible preachers. To condemn the many for the errors of a few would add a second injustice to the first.

sa.prompt: How has the movement itself responded to the prosperity message, and what does that show?
sa.model: Pentecostal and charismatic theologians, pastors, and even official denominational statements have publicly rejected the prosperity message and the excesses of positive confession as a corruption of the gospel of grace. The sharpest critics of health-and-wealth teaching are often found not outside the movement but within it, among believers who love the work of the Spirit and grieve to see His name attached to a message of mere gain. A body that names and disowns the error in its own midst shows the marks of health, not sickness; this too is a reason to weigh the movement by its faithful and its Scriptures and to refuse the easy caricature that paints the whole with the colors of its worst.
